blocks.text: The module documentation defines proposal/result ordering, ownership matching, idempotency, disconnect and cancellation hooks, output limits, trust labels, approval observation, retention, and logging restrictions.
blocks.title: Broker lifecycle and trust contract

blocks.text: ToolOutcome is the loop-facing immutable result. Helpers cap UTF-8 output, normalize device ids, validate scalar fields, consume failed futures, and provide process-wide emitter and connection lookups.
blocks.title: Outcome and validation helpers

blocks.text: _Call retains ownership identity, original connection, timing, completion future, approval callback, duplicate and late counters, and stream byte totals.
blocks.title: Per-call state

blocks.text: ToolBroker validates injected collaborators and limits, stores callbacks and trust configuration, creates call/stat/task state, and prepares stable router handler objects.
blocks.title: Broker construction

blocks.text: propose validates and deduplicates calls, enforces per-run in-flight limits, rejects offline devices as disconnected outcomes, registers new calls, and spawns proposal/deadline tasks.

blocks.text: _close marks the first completion synchronously and schedules announcement. _finish waits for it, _announce emits tool_finished before resolving waiters, and timeout sends a fixed device error.

blocks.text: Run and connection hooks close pending calls. Result, approval, and stream handlers validate payloads, enforce connection ownership, apply output limits, notify callbacks, and preserve first-outcome behavior.

gotchas: The broker never makes approval policy decisions.
A disconnected device is not silently revived on reconnect.
Proposal emission failures are raised, but finish-event failures are recorded in the outcome.
how_it_works: Registers calls by run and call id

purpose: The broker is the server-side exchange for tools executed by a connected device. It validates ownership and payloads, emits proposals, handles results, approvals, streams, timeout, cancellation, and disconnect, and exposes bounded in-memory idempotency and statistics.
summary: Coordinates device tool calls from proposal through exactly one outcome and tool-finished event.
